classification.difficultyReason: Foundation: explain directly from the measured quantity that the tallest time bar indicates the longest run time and therefore the slowest runner. This contextual reversal is explicitly taught.

inlines.text: The bar chart shows the times taken by a group of students to run 100m
Lydia says, "Ed is the best runner because his bar is the tallest."

spec.description: Native editable reconstruction of the source column positions with six names, arrowed axes and a 0–30 scale labelled every 5 seconds. The title wraps at the units to preserve readable labels. Decorative cyan fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Approximate source positions: Zach about 21 s, Benji about 18 s, Emily about 14 s, Faith about 25 s, Ed about 27 s and Seb about 22 s. These are drawing estimates, not exact givens. Ed has the longest time and Emily the shortest.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied comparison graph remains visible. No numerical value labels or conclusion are added to the question.

answer.short: Ed was the slowest because he took the longest time to run 100 m.
answer.worked: The vertical scale shows time taken to run the same distance. Ed’s tallest bar means he took the longest time, so he was the slowest. A shorter time means a faster runner.
